glosses: To estimate too low; to perceive (someone or something) as having a lower value, quantity, worth, etc., than what he/she/it actually has.

To state (something) with less completeness than needed; to minimise or downplay.

examples.text: To call it a calculated bet understates the risk; it is a Hail Mary pass.

glosses: To state (something) with a lack of emphasis, in order to express irony.
To state a quantity that is too low.

examples.text: The company had been understating its liabilities for years.

glosses: To make smaller.

examples.text: Schneckenburger strives to make it appear that Baur unduly minifies the Christian element in Manichæism.

glosses: To reduce in apparent size, as for example objects viewed through a lens or mirror shaped so as to increase the field of view, such as a convex or aspheric mirror or a Fresnel lens.

examples.text: But, mused Parker, this theory of one's perplexities being diminished by the vastly superior height of these Gothic arches cannot have any foundation in fact, for the same inverted telescope that minifies my burdens also minifies my capacity to carry them, leaving me exactly of the same stature as before.

glosses: To remove white space and unnecessary characters from source code in order to reduce its size.

examples.text: When code is minified, all comments are removed, as well as unneeded whitespace characters (space, newline, and tab).

examples.text: We have to minimize the budget.

examples.text: The insurance adjuster tried to minimize the extent of the damage to lessen the company's exposure to liability.

glosses: To remove (a window) from the main display area, collapsing it to an icon or caption.

examples.text: I didn't close anything, but I minimized all the windows so I could see the desktop.

glosses: To treat (someone) in a slighting manner.

examples.text: […] father who had never openly minimized him or anything he did […]
